question: In the practice area of Life Insurance, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'participating pension product with dynamic bonus declarations' involving bonus smoothing and policyholder reasonable expectations (PRE), the actuary is determining whether an understatement in liability calculations requires disclosure. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Assess materiality from the perspective of the intended user; an omission or understatement is material if it could reasonably influence the user's decision-making.
Assume no error can ever be material if the client's balance sheet is certified by a CA.
Set materiality equal to a fixed flat amount of Rs. 100 regardless of the size of the entity.
Evaluate materiality solely based on whether the error reduces the actuary's consulting fee.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.4 (Materiality Assessment from User Perspective)), the correct standard requirement is: Assess materiality from the perspective of the intended user; an omission or understatement is material if it could reasonably influence the user's decision-making.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

source: APS 34 Practice Standard (Section 2.5 (Data Quality: Sufficient and Reliable Data))
question: In the practice area of Life Insurance, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'participating pension product with dynamic bonus declarations' involving bonus smoothing and policyholder reasonable expectations (PRE), the actuary is evaluating historical policyholder records provided by the client. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Take reasonable steps to review completeness, consistency, and accuracy (reconciliation to audited statements, reasonableness tests, and prior period comparisons).
Assume all client data is 100% perfect without conducting any validation or reasonableness checks.
Discard 50% of the data at random to make calculations run faster on the computer.
Accept unverified verbal data estimates from the client's marketing manager.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.5 (Data Quality: Sufficient and Reliable Data)), the correct standard requirement is: Take reasonable steps to review completeness, consistency, and accuracy (reconciliation to audited statements, reasonableness tests, and prior period comparisons).
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

source: APS 34 Practice Standard (Section 2.7.5 (Individual vs Aggregate Reasonableness of Assumptions))
question: In the practice area of Life Insurance, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'participating pension product with dynamic bonus declarations' involving bonus smoothing and policyholder reasonable expectations (PRE), the actuary is setting a suite of economic and demographic assumptions. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Use assumptions chosen by a random number generator to prove mathematical neutrality.
Assess whether the assumption set is reasonable in the aggregate, ensuring that multiple individually prudent assumptions do not distort the total result.
Average all assumptions together into a single composite number.
Ensure every individual assumption is set at maximum extreme pessimism, compounding into an unrealistic aggregate reserve.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.7.5 (Individual vs Aggregate Reasonableness of Assumptions)), the correct standard requirement is: Assess whether the assumption set is reasonable in the aggregate, ensuring that multiple individually prudent assumptions do not distort the total result.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

options: Ensure every individual assumption is set at maximum extreme pessimism, compounding into an unrealistic aggregate reserve.
Assess whether the assumption set is reasonable in the aggregate, ensuring that multiple individually prudent assumptions do not distort the total result.
Average all assumptions together into a single composite number.
Use assumptions chosen by a random number generator to prove mathematical neutrality.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.7.5 (Individual vs Aggregate Reasonableness of Assumptions)), the correct standard requirement is: Assess whether the assumption set is reasonable in the aggregate, ensuring that multiple individually prudent assumptions do not distort the total result.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

source: APS 34 Practice Standard (Section 2.8 (Prescribed Assumptions Not Supported by Actuary))
question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'gratuity valuation under Ind AS 19 / AS 15' involving salary escalation rates, attrition rates, and discount curves, the actuary is evaluating an assumption mandated by the client company's board of directors. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Refuse to complete the report and file a police complaint against the board of directors.
Quietly modify the assumption in the computer model without telling the board.
Pretend the actuary chose the assumption independently to protect the board from embarrassment.
If unwilling to support the prescribed assumption, disclose that fact, the party who prescribed it, and the reasons why that party set the assumption.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.8 (Prescribed Assumptions Not Supported by Actuary)), the correct standard requirement is: If unwilling to support the prescribed assumption, disclose that fact, the party who prescribed it, and the reasons why that party set the assumption.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'gratuity valuation under Ind AS 19 / AS 15' involving salary escalation rates, attrition rates, and discount curves, the actuary is validating a complex new valuation spreadsheet platform. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Have the lead programmer validate their own spreadsheet code in self-review.
Validate the model by checking only whether the title slide looks visually attractive.
Ensure validation is performed by individuals who did not develop the model, assessing fit for purpose, specification compliance, and reproducibility.
Assume computer models never contain errors because software is automated.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.10.2 (Independent Model Validation)), the correct standard requirement is: Ensure validation is performed by individuals who did not develop the model, assessing fit for purpose, specification compliance, and reproducibility.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

source: APS 34 Practice Standard (Section 2.12 (Peer Review Protocol & Independence))
question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'gratuity valuation under Ind AS 19 / AS 15' involving salary escalation rates, attrition rates, and discount curves, the actuary is arranging an independent review of an actuarial valuation report. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Peer review is prohibited under APS 34 to protect confidential intellectual property.
Select a junior student trainee who worked on data entry for the same project.
Select an independent reviewer knowledgeable and experienced in the practice area, who was not involved in the work under review.
Select the client's Chief Financial Officer as the actuarial peer reviewer.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.12 (Peer Review Protocol & Independence)), the correct standard requirement is: Select an independent reviewer knowledgeable and experienced in the practice area, who was not involved in the work under review.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

source: APS 34 Practice Standard (Section 2.14 (Retention of Documentation & The Peer Replicability Test))
question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'gratuity valuation under Ind AS 19 / AS 15' involving salary escalation rates, attrition rates, and discount curves, the actuary is archiving actuarial working papers and calculation models. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Keep records in the actuary's personal memory without writing anything down.
Store documentation on temporary scratch paper that is erased weekly.
Retain working papers for exactly 30 days before permanently shredding all files.
Retain documentation for a reasonable period with enough detail for another qualified actuary in the same practice area to replicate the work and evaluate judgments.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.14 (Retention of Documentation & The Peer Replicability Test)), the correct standard requirement is: Retain documentation for a reasonable period with enough detail for another qualified actuary in the same practice area to replicate the work and evaluate judgments.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'leave encashment and post-retirement medical benefit schemes' involving medical inflation, leave utilization rates, and service tenure, the actuary is deciding whether an indicated action is an unconditional obligation. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: 'Must' applies only to actuarial trainees, while Fellows are exempt.
'Must' and 'Should' are interchangeable stylistic synonyms with zero technical difference.
'Must' is purely aspirational, while 'Should' is legally enforceable under criminal law.
'Must' denotes an absolute mandatory requirement; 'Should' denotes standard expected practice with rebuttable presumption requiring explicit documented departure.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 1.6.1 (Language: 'Must' vs 'Should')), the correct standard requirement is: 'Must' denotes an absolute mandatory requirement; 'Should' denotes standard expected practice with rebuttable presumption requiring explicit documented departure.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

source: APS 34 Practice Standard (Section 2.1 (Acceptance of Assignment & Terms of Reference))
question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'leave encashment and post-retirement medical benefit schemes' involving medical inflation, leave utilization rates, and service tenure, the actuary is formalizing the scope, constraints, and resources for an actuarial assignment. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Begin calculations immediately without written terms of reference to maximize project speed.
Delegate all terms of reference negotiation to junior administrative clerks.
Confirm the role of principal, constraints, expected schedule/costs, and ensure competence and PCS/APS compliance before accepting.
Agree to whatever outcome the client demands in exchange for upfront payment of fees.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.1 (Acceptance of Assignment & Terms of Reference)), the correct standard requirement is: Confirm the role of principal, constraints, expected schedule/costs, and ensure competence and PCS/APS compliance before accepting.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'leave encashment and post-retirement medical benefit schemes' involving medical inflation, leave utilization rates, and service tenure, the actuary is using financial projections prepared by an external investment banking expert. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: State reliance on the expert and disclaim responsibility, disclosing the source, extent of reliance, and steps taken to examine for obvious shortcomings.
Accept the investment banker's numbers without review and present them as the actuary's own work.
Disclaim responsibility verbally during a phone call while remaining silent in the written report.
Delete all reference to the investment banker to claim sole authorship of the projections.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.3 (Reliance on Others: Disclaiming Responsibility)), the correct standard requirement is: State reliance on the expert and disclaim responsibility, disclosing the source, extent of reliance, and steps taken to examine for obvious shortcomings.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'leave encashment and post-retirement medical benefit schemes' involving medical inflation, leave utilization rates, and service tenure, the actuary is determining whether an understatement in liability calculations requires disclosure. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Evaluate materiality solely based on whether the error reduces the actuary's consulting fee.
Assess materiality from the perspective of the intended user; an omission or understatement is material if it could reasonably influence the user's decision-making.
Assume no error can ever be material if the client's balance sheet is certified by a CA.
Set materiality equal to a fixed flat amount of Rs. 100 regardless of the size of the entity.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.4 (Materiality Assessment from User Perspective)), the correct standard requirement is: Assess materiality from the perspective of the intended user; an omission or understatement is material if it could reasonably influence the user's decision-making.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

question: In the practice area of Pensions & Employee Benefits, while performing an actuarial assignment on 'leave encashment and post-retirement medical benefit schemes' involving medical inflation, leave utilization rates, and service tenure, the actuary is evaluating historical policyholder records provided by the client. Under APS 34 (General Actuarial Practice Standard), what is the mandatory requirement?
options: Accept unverified verbal data estimates from the client's marketing manager.
Take reasonable steps to review completeness, consistency, and accuracy (reconciliation to audited statements, reasonableness tests, and prior period comparisons).
Assume all client data is 100% perfect without conducting any validation or reasonableness checks.
Discard 50% of the data at random to make calculations run faster on the computer.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 (Section 2.5 (Data Quality: Sufficient and Reliable Data)), the correct standard requirement is: Take reasonable steps to review completeness, consistency, and accuracy (reconciliation to audited statements, reasonableness tests, and prior period comparisons).
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate foundational principles of APS 34 (ISAP 1) regarding actuarial judgment, documentation, or disclosure.

No disclosure is required because internal working assumptions are proprietary trade secrets.
The actuary is legally prohibited from mentioning assumptions in any written communication.
The disclosure should be given verbally to the receptionist and omitted from the formal report.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 34 Section 3.2.2, the mandatory disclosure requirement is: Disclose that the assumption was mandated by law/regulation and note whether it limits relevance for other financial purposes.
explanationIncorrect: Omitting mandatory disclosures under Section 3.2.2 violates APS 34 and misleads intended users.

options: verifying immediate P&L recognition and establishing a systematically tracked loss component within LRC
offsetting onerous group losses against profits from unrelated groups to avoid P&L charges
capitalizing the initial onerous deficit as an intangible goodwill asset on the balance sheet
delaying onerous loss recognition until claims exceed premium collections
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and Ind AS 117 (Onerous Contract Grouping & Loss Component Tracking (Para 47)), the correct audit requirement is: verifying immediate P&L recognition and establishing a systematically tracked loss component within LRC. This ensures rigorous compliance with ICAI SA 620 and statutory valuation standards.
explanationIncorrect: The alternative actions violate core auditing principles: Option B (offsetting onerous group losses against ...), Option C (capitalizing the initial onerous deficit...), and Option D (delaying onerous loss recognition until ...) breach ICAI standards or Ind AS 117.

source: FT-IGN 31 & Ind AS 117 (Working Paper Access Asymmetry (FT-IGN 31 Sec 3.19.5))
question: During a statutory Ind AS 117 audit of a Health Insurer issuing 'Individual Health Indemnity Insurance (Annual Renewable)' measured under the Premium Allocation Approach (PAA), the Auditing Actuary is managing statutory auditor and client management requests to inspect internal audit working papers. Considering that this portfolio involves medical inflation, hospital billing disputes, and aging curve morbidity adjustments, what is the mandatory requirement under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620?
options: uploading internal audit challenge memos to the company's public intranet
withholding working papers from the statutory audit partner to protect actuarial secrecy
handing over internal auditor challenge memos to client management upon executive demand
providing unrestricted access to the statutory auditor while strictly withholding internal challenge memos from client management
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and Ind AS 117 (Working Paper Access Asymmetry (FT-IGN 31 Sec 3.19.5)), the correct audit requirement is: providing unrestricted access to the statutory auditor while strictly withholding internal challenge memos from client management. This ensures rigorous compliance with ICAI SA 620 and statutory valuation standards.
explanationIncorrect: The alternative actions violate core auditing principles: Option B (handing over internal auditor challenge ...), Option C (withholding working papers from the stat...), and Option D (uploading internal audit challenge memos...) breach ICAI standards or Ind AS 117.

explanationIncorrect: The alternative actions violate core auditing principles: Option B (bypassing the Audit Committee and immedi...), Option C (surrendering the audit objection immedia...), and Option D (escalating directly to the Supreme Court...) breach ICAI standards or Ind AS 117.

options: Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.
Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Super-Imposed Judicial Inflation in Motor TP (Sec 5.17))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is projecting future claim inflation for motor bodily injury claims. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Apply a negative inflation rate to compress long-tail reserving deficits.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund.
Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Foreign Exchange Accounting (Ind AS 21 & 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is auditing foreign currency denominated insurance contracts in GIFT City. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses.
Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements.
Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published.
Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements.
Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits.

Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards.
Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features.
Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Foreign Exchange Accounting (Ind AS 21 & 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is auditing foreign currency denominated insurance contracts in GIFT City. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses.
Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Interim Accounting Policy Choice (Para B137))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits.
Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published.
Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements.
Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Transition Fair Value Model (Para C20))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening CSM determined under the Fair Value Approach at transition. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance.
Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court.
Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a joint audit conducted by two independent statutory audit firms, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks.
Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

options: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books.
Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses.
Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Interim Accounting Policy Choice (Para B137))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published.
Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits.
Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements.
Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Transition Fair Value Model (Para C20))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is auditing opening CSM determined under the Fair Value Approach at transition. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance.
Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.
Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable.
Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Super-Imposed Judicial Inflation in Motor TP (Sec 5.17))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is projecting future claim inflation for motor bodily injury claims. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Apply a negative inflation rate to compress long-tail reserving deficits.
Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of unit-linked funds with guaranteed minimum death benefits (GMDB), the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes.
Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while evaluating compliance with IRDAI-prescribed CCIL yield curve discounting circulars, the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule.
All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while evaluating compliance with IRDAI-prescribed CCIL yield curve discounting circulars, the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features.
Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Options B, C, and D violate statutory requirements under Ind AS 117 or ICAI auditing standards.
