question: Before an actuarial firm accepts a complex multi-line insurance audit engagement, what governance step is required under ICAI SA 220 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.2?
options: The firm must obtain approval from all competing actuarial firms in Mumbai.
The firm must take out a life insurance policy on the client's Chief Risk Officer.
The firm must submit the resume of every junior trainee to the Central Government for police clearance.
The firm's risk and quality leadership must conduct a formal pre-acceptance review evaluating team capacity, technical competence in Ind AS 117, and absence of independence conflicts.
explanationCorrect: Under SA 220 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.2, formal client acceptance and continuance evaluations must be performed to ensure independence, competence, and adequate resource availability.
explanationIncorrect: Accepting engagements without adequate technical competence in Ind AS 117 violates foundational quality management standards.

question: Under ICAI Standard on Auditing SA 230 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.19, who legally owns the working papers prepared by the Auditing Actuary?
options: The working papers are the property of the Auditing Actuary / statutory auditor and remain in their exclusive legal custody.
The working papers belong to the policyholders and must be uploaded to a public website.
The working papers are the statutory property of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
The working papers are the property of the insurance company management and must be surrendered upon request.
explanationCorrect: Under ICAI SA 230 Para 14 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.19, audit working papers, challenge memos, and calculations are the property of the audit firm / expert, not the client entity.
explanationIncorrect: Clients have a right to audit conclusions and reports, but do not own internal audit working papers.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.19.3 (Content of Actuarial Challenge Memos)
question: What must be recorded in an 'Actuarial Challenge Memo' prepared by the Auditing Actuary during an Ind AS 117 audit?
options: Personal insults regarding the competence of the insurer's junior actuarial students.
A transcript of the actuary's casual coffee break conversations with office staff.
Only the final agreed numbers, deleting all records of initial objections or discrepancies.
The specific balance questioned, the underlying data analyzed, management's rationale, the alternative assumptions tested, the quantitative impact, and the final resolution or remaining disagreement.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.19.3, challenge memos must document the full audit trail: the initial concern, supporting evidence, management discussions, alternative calculations, and basis of resolution.
explanationIncorrect: Deleting or concealing initial audit objections violates SA 230 documentation requirements.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.19.6 (Management Pushback against Access Asymmetry)
question: An insurance company's Board Audit Committee refuses to approve the audit fee unless the Auditing Actuary hands over all internal challenge memos exchanged with the statutory auditor. How should the actuary respond?
options: Firmly refuse; explain that access asymmetry is a statutory auditing safeguard under SA 230 / SA 620 to protect auditor independence, and escalate to the Statutory Audit Partner.
Sue the Audit Committee for extortion under criminal law.
Burn all working papers to prevent either party from reading them.
Immediately hand over all files to ensure prompt payment of invoices.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.19.5, management has no legal right to demand internal challenge memos exchanged between the auditor and their expert. Handing them over breaches audit confidentiality.
explanationIncorrect: Audit independence requires an uninhibited internal communication channel between the auditor and expert.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.19.7 (Assembly and Archiving of the Final Audit File)
question: Under ICAI SA 230 Para 14, within what timeframe after the auditor's report date must the Auditing Actuary assemble and lock the final actuarial audit working paper file?
options: Exactly 5 years after the completion of the audit.
Ordinarily not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report (the audit file assembly period).
Within 24 hours of issuing the draft opinion.
There is no deadline; files can be edited and modified indefinitely over decades.
explanationCorrect: Under ICAI SA 230, the final audit file must be assembled, closed, and locked within 60 days of the audit report date, after which no deletions or alterations are permitted.
explanationIncorrect: Retroactively modifying or adding working papers after the assembly deadline without formal documentation violates SA 230.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.19.8 (Subsequent Modification of Audit Files)
question: If an Auditing Actuary finds it necessary to clarify an existing working paper after the final audit file has been locked, what is required under SA 230 Para 16?
options: Silently overwrite the file using administrative computer passwords to erase any record of change.
Document the specific reasons for making the changes, when and by whom they were made and reviewed, while retaining the original unedited record.
Delete the entire folder and claim the files were destroyed by a computer virus.
Pay a penalty fee of Rs. 50,000 to the Disciplinary Directorate.
explanationCorrect: Under SA 230 Para 16, post-assembly modifications require full documentation of reasons, date, author, and reviewer, preserving the complete unedited historical audit trail.
explanationIncorrect: Covertly altering locked audit files constitutes tampering with audit evidence and severe professional misconduct.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.20, what is a 'Cold Quality Review' in the context of actuarial audit engagements?
options: An inspection of completed audit files conducted after the audit report has been issued, performed by partners or experts who had no involvement in the audit.
A review of deceased policyholders' death claims by medical doctors.
A review conducted exclusively during winter months in North India.
A review of financial records conducted in refrigerated temperature-controlled rooms.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.20 and ICAI SQC 1, cold reviews are post-issuance quality assurance inspections carried out by independent reviewers to ensure adherence to professional standards.
explanationIncorrect: Cold reviews provide feedback on audit rigor, documentation quality, and compliance with FT-IGN 31.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.21.1 (Communication with Engagement Quality Reviewer)
question: When must the Auditing Actuary formally communicate with the Engagement Quality Control Reviewer (EQCR)?
options: Exclusively after the company has published its annual report in the newspapers.
Only when the client agrees to pay an additional quality fee.
Only if the statutory auditor has resigned from the engagement.
On all significant actuarial matters, contentious valuation decisions, unresolved audit differences, and the proposed audit conclusions prior to report sign-off.
explanationCorrect: Under SA 220 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.21, the EQCR must be briefed on all significant risks, challenge memos, and judgment calls before the final audit opinion is released.
explanationIncorrect: The EQCR cannot sign off on the audit without reviewing the resolution of all material actuarial challenges.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.21.3 (Documenting Differences of Opinion with EQCR)
question: What must happen if the Auditing Actuary and the EQCR have an unresolved difference of opinion regarding an Ind AS 117 valuation treatment?
options: The insurer's Managing Director decides which valuation method is more convenient.
The Auditing Actuary can ignore the EQCR and instruct the auditor to sign immediately.
The junior audit trainee flips a coin to decide whose opinion prevails.
The audit report cannot be issued until the difference of opinion is formally resolved following the firm's established dispute resolution procedures.
explanationCorrect: Under SA 220 Para 21, when differences of opinion arise between the engagement partner and the EQCR, the engagement report shall not be dated until the difference is resolved.
explanationIncorrect: Bypassing the EQCR to issue an audit report violates core audit quality control standards.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.22.2 (Written Representations from Management - SA 580)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.22 and ICAI SA 580, what specific written representations must the Auditing Actuary ensure are obtained from insurer management?
options: That management has provided all relevant data and models, that assumptions reflect management's best estimate intent, and that unadjusted actuarial differences are immaterial.
That all policyholders will renew their policies for the next 10 years without fail.
That the insurer promises never to contest any future tax assessments.
That the statutory auditors are immune from all legal scrutiny in civil courts.
explanationCorrect: Under SA 580 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.22, written management representations confirm completeness of data, validity of assumptions, and agreement that unadjusted misstatements are immaterial.
explanationIncorrect: Management representations complement audit procedures but do not substitute for independent audit evidence.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.22.4 (Communication of Unadjusted Audit Differences)
question: What must the Auditing Actuary do regarding actuarial differences that management refuses to adjust in the financial statements?
options: Force the Appointed Actuary to pay the difference out of their personal salary.
Shred the schedule so the Board of Directors does not become alarmed.
Secretly deduct the difference from the client's next consulting invoice.
Compile an 'Aggregate Schedule of Unadjusted Audit Differences', assess their cumulative materiality, and report them to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG).
explanationCorrect: Under SA 450 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.22, all uncorrected misstatements must be accumulated, evaluated for individual and aggregate materiality, and formally communicated to the Audit Committee / TCWG.
explanationIncorrect: Unadjusted differences above the performance materiality threshold may necessitate a qualified or modified audit opinion.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.1 (Level 1: Working Level Resolution Mechanics)
question: At Level 1 of the FT-IGN 31 disagreement escalation pathway, what is the required interaction between the Auditing Actuary and the Appointed Actuary?
options: Direct technical discussions, model re-runs, and sharing of empirical data to test whether differences can be reconciled within actuarial tolerance bands.
Filing cross-complaints with the Director (Discipline) of the IAI within 24 hours.
Publishing competing articles in the Actuary India magazine criticizing each other's methodologies.
Demanding that IRDAI immediately suspend the Appointed Actuary's Certificate of Practice.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.1, Level 1 focuses on professional, objective technical dialogue between the actuaries to explore data, test sensitivities, and resolve technical differences amicably.
explanationIncorrect: Premature escalation to external bodies without attempting working-level professional reconciliation violates due process.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.2 (Level 2: Audit Partner & Ind AS 117 Lead Escalation)
question: When should a dispute be escalated from Level 1 to Level 2 under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.2?
options: Only after the financial year has ended and the annual report has been printed.
When technical discussions between the actuaries reach an impasse on a matter with a potentially material impact on financial statements.
Whenever the Appointed Actuary takes a leave of absence for personal reasons.
Only if the disagreement involves an amount under Rs. 1,000.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.2, when working-level discussions cannot reconcile a material difference, the matter is formally elevated to the Audit Engagement Partner and the Insurer's Ind AS Lead.
explanationIncorrect: Level 2 introduces senior audit leadership to resolve technical impasses before formal board reporting.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.3 (Level 3: EQCR & Audit Committee Involvement)
question: What triggers Level 3 escalation under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.3, and who is brought into the discussion?
options: A drop in the company's share price on the stock exchange.
The appointment of a new brand ambassador for the insurance company.
A request by the company's junior clerks for higher overtime compensation.
Failure to resolve the issue at Level 2; the matter is escalated to the Engagement Quality Control Reviewer (EQCR under SA 220) and the Audit Committee of the Board.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.3, Level 3 elevates the dispute to the governance level: the firm's EQCR and the insurer's Audit Committee, bringing independent oversight to bear.
explanationIncorrect: The Audit Committee is legally responsible for financial reporting integrity and must be appraised of significant actuarial disagreements.

question: What occurs at Level 4 of the FT-IGN 31 dispute escalation pathway?
options: A televised debate between the Appointed Actuary and the Auditing Actuary.
Commercial arbitration conducted under the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) in Paris.
A public referendum among all registered policyholders of the insurer.
Formal presentation by the Statutory Auditor and Auditing Actuary to the Board of Directors / Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) warning of impending audit report modification.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.4, Level 4 is the final internal governance stage: presenting the material misstatement to the full Board of Directors, warning that failure to adjust will lead to audit qualification.
explanationIncorrect: The Board must be given the opportunity to require management to adjust the financial statements before external reporting.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.5 (Level 5: Trigger for Regulatory Notification)
question: When does Level 5 escalation under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23 become mandatory?
options: Only if the insurer goes into liquidation and ceases operations.
Whenever the insurer changes its corporate logo or website layout.
When the Board of Directors refuses to correct a material misstatement, leaving the financial statements materially false or misleading, compelling notification to IRDAI and IAI.
When the Appointed Actuary forgets to submit their annual CPD self-attestation.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.5, if the Board refuses to correct a material distortion that compromises the true and fair view, the auditor and expert must report the matter to statutory regulators.
explanationIncorrect: Level 5 is the ultimate regulatory safeguard to protect policyholders, financial stability, and public interest.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.7 (Auditing Actuary's Legal Protection at Level 5)
question: What legal protection does the Auditing Actuary have when reporting an uncorrected misstatement to IRDAI at Level 5?
options: The actuary is legally protected because disclosure under statutory regulatory duties and in the public interest overrides contractual client confidentiality.
The actuary can only be protected if they surrender their Indian citizenship.
The actuary has no legal protection and is personally liable for all client losses in tort.
The actuary must obtain a signed letter of indemnity from the President of India.
explanationCorrect: Under PCS v4.0 Para 3.2 and Section 19 of the Actuaries Act, statutory regulatory reporting in the public interest is a recognized legal exception to client confidentiality.
explanationIncorrect: Members cannot be disciplined for fulfilling mandatory statutory reporting duties to regulators.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.8 (Documentation of the Escalation Trail)
question: What documentation must the Auditing Actuary preserve regarding the 5-step dispute escalation process?
options: No documentation is needed once the dispute is escalated to the Board.
Only informal notes kept on personal mobile phone messaging apps.
Only the final newspaper clipping reporting the company's financial results.
A complete contemporaneous record of all meetings, written challenge memos, technical responses from management, minutes of Audit Committee discussions, and formal correspondence.
explanationCorrect: Under ICAI SA 230 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23.8, thorough contemporaneous documentation of every escalation stage is critical to demonstrate audit due diligence and defend the expert's conclusions.
explanationIncorrect: Inadequate documentation of dispute escalation exposes the audit team to regulatory sanctions and disciplinary scrutiny.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.9 (Audit Opinion Impact: Qualified vs Adverse vs Disclaimer)
question: If a material actuarial misstatement remains uncorrected at Level 4 and is both material and pervasive to the financial statements, what audit opinion must the statutory auditor issue?
options: An Adverse Audit Opinion, stating that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view.
A provisional opinion subject to future lottery drawings.
A certificate of appreciation for the Appointed Actuary.
An Unmodified Clean Opinion with a congratulatory note to management.
explanationCorrect: Under ICAI SA 705, when uncorrected misstatements are both material and pervasive, an Adverse Opinion is mandatory. If material but not pervasive, a Qualified Opinion is issued.
explanationIncorrect: Issuing a clean opinion when pervasive actuarial misstatements exist constitutes gross audit negligence.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.10 (Resignation as Auditor's Expert as Last Resort)
question: Under what circumstances should the Auditing Actuary consider withdrawing/resigning from the audit engagement under FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23?
options: Whenever the client requests a meeting during a weekend.
If the weather in the client's city is unpleasantly hot.
Where management imposes scope limitations that prevent obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence, or where management integrity is fundamentally compromised.
Whenever the audit team finishes their work ahead of schedule.
explanationCorrect: Under SA 620 Para A34 and FT-IGN 31 Section 3.23, severe management-imposed scope limitations or fraudulent misrepresentations may force the expert to conclude that resignation is the only ethical course.
explanationIncorrect: Withdrawal must be accompanied by formal communication to the statutory auditor and, where required, regulatory notifications.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 3.23.11 (Disciplinary Referral for Professional Misconduct)
question: If the Auditing Actuary uncovers that the Appointed Actuary deliberately falsified data or concealed negative reserve margins, what duty arises under PCS v4.0 and FT-IGN 31?
options: The Auditing Actuary must escalate through the audit hierarchy and, if unrectified, lodge a formal disciplinary complaint with the Director (Discipline) of the IAI.
The Auditing Actuary must demand a 50% share of the company's profits in exchange for silence.
The Auditing Actuary must ignore the falsification because peer actuaries must always protect each other.
The Auditing Actuary must assist the Appointed Actuary in concealing the fraud from the statutory auditor.
explanationCorrect: Under PCS v4.0 Para 5.2 and FT-IGN 31, discovering deliberate fraud or gross professional misconduct by a peer creates an ethical obligation to ensure proper regulatory and disciplinary reporting.
explanationIncorrect: Colluding in data falsification or concealing material fraud constitutes severe misconduct punishable by permanent expulsion.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.1 (General Measurement Model - GMM Building Blocks)
question: What are the four fundamental building blocks of the General Measurement Model (GMM) under Ind AS 117 audited by the Auditing Actuary?
options: Estimates of future cash flows, adjustment for time value of money (discounting), Risk Adjustment for non-financial risk (RA), and Contractual Service Margin (CSM).
Premium income, commission expense, management expenses, and income tax provision.
Unearned premium reserve, additional reserve, claims incurred but not reported, and catastrophe margin.
Book value of assets, market value of equities, paid-up share capital, and statutory dividend reserves.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 32 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.1, GMM comprises Fulfilment Cash Flows (present value of future cash flows plus Risk Adjustment) plus the Contractual Service Margin (unearned profit).
explanationIncorrect: Historical UPR and claims reserves under Ind AS 104 are replaced by the forward-looking building block architecture of Ind AS 117.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.3 (Premium Allocation Approach - PAA Safe Harbour)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 53(b) and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.3, what is the exact criterion for an insurance contract to automatically qualify for the simplified PAA without testing?
options: The coverage period of each contract in the group (including coverage arising from all premiums within contract boundary) is one year or less at initial recognition.
The contract is written by a non-life insurer regardless of the policy duration.
The total annual premium is less than Rs. 1 Crore.
The policyholder is an individual citizen rather than a corporate entity.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 53(b), the PAA safe harbour applies if and only if the coverage period of the whole contract is 1 year or less at inception.
explanationIncorrect: Contracts with coverage periods exceeding 1 year require rigorous quantitative eligibility testing against GMM to qualify for PAA.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.4 (PAA Eligibility Testing for Contracts > 1 Year)
question: How must an insurer prove PAA eligibility for a 2-year warranty policy that does not qualify for the 1-year safe harbour under Ind AS 117 Para 53(a)?
options: By obtaining a written exemption certificate from the local Chamber of Commerce.
By showing that the policyholder paid the entire 2-year premium upfront in cash.
By demonstrating that PAA measurement would not produce a measurement of the Liability for Remaining Coverage (LRC) that differs materially from that produced by the General Measurement Model.
By proving that no claims occurred during the first 6 months of coverage.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 53(a) and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.4, multi-year contracts qualify for PAA only if the insurer proves that LRC under PAA is not materially different from GMM under reasonable scenarios.
explanationIncorrect: If significant variability in cash flows is expected before claims are incurred, PAA eligibility is failed and GMM must be applied.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.6 (Variable Fee Approach - VFA Direct Participation Criteria)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B101 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.6, what three criteria must be met for a unit-linked contract to be audited under the Variable Fee Approach (VFA)?
options: The contract must be sold exclusively through internet banking portals.

Contract terms specify policyholder participation in a clearly identified pool of assets; entity expects to pay substantial share of fair value returns; entity expects substantial proportion of cash flow changes to vary with fair value.
The contract must have zero mortality charges and zero expense deductions.
The policyholder must be a high-net-worth individual with over Rs. 10 Crores in assets.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para B101, VFA applies to direct participating contracts where policyholder returns are fundamentally tied to a designated pool of underlying items, with the insurer acting as investment manager.
explanationIncorrect: If any of the three direct participation criteria is absent, the contract must be measured under the standard GMM.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.8 (Auditing Contractual Service Margin - CSM Release)
question: How does the Auditing Actuary audit the release of Contractual Service Margin (CSM) to the profit or loss statement under Ind AS 117 Para B119?
options: Verify that the entire CSM is recognized as upfront profit on the day the policy is issued.
Ensure that CSM is released only when the policyholder passes away or surrenders the policy.
Verify that CSM is systematically recognized over the coverage period based on 'coverage units', reflecting the quantity of benefits provided and expected duration of coverage in each period.
Ensure that CSM is recognized in equal monthly installments over exactly 50 years regardless of contract term.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para B119 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.8, CSM represents unearned profit and must be recognized in profit or loss over current and future coverage periods based on coverage units provided.
explanationIncorrect: Recognizing CSM upfront at inception violates Ind AS 117 and results in fraudulent overstatement of early-year profits.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.10 (CSM Unlocking: Financial vs Non-Financial Changes)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Paras 44-45 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.10, which assumption changes unlock (adjust) the CSM under GMM, and which flow directly to P&L?
options: Interest rate changes unlock CSM, while mortality changes flow to P&L.
CSM can never be adjusted after initial recognition under any circumstances.

Changes in estimates of future cash flows and RA relating to future service unlock CSM; changes related to past/current service and effects of time value of money (interest rates) flow directly to P&L.
All assumption changes flow exclusively to the balance sheet with zero P&L impact.
explanationCorrect: Under GMM, changes in fulfilment cash flows relating to future coverage adjust the CSM (so long as CSM is positive). Changes relating to current/past service and discount rates impact P&L / OCI directly.
explanationIncorrect: Misclassifying assumption changes between CSM unlocking and direct P&L recognition distorts reported operating performance.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.12 (Auditing Loss Component for Onerous Contracts)
question: When a group of insurance contracts is determined to be onerous at initial recognition under Ind AS 117 Para 47, how must it be audited?
options: Capitalize the initial loss as an intangible asset to be amortized over 20 years.
Record the loss as a negative dividend payable to equity shareholders.
Allow management to defer the loss and offset it against profits from other profitable groups.
Ensure a loss is recognized immediately in profit or loss for the net cash outflow, establishing a 'loss component' within the LRC that reduces subsequent revenue recognition.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 47 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.12, onerous contracts cannot have a positive CSM; the net outflow must be recognized immediately in P&L, creating a tracked loss component.
explanationIncorrect: Cross-subsidizing onerous contracts against profitable groups violates the strict grouping requirements of Ind AS 117 Para 16.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.14 (Level of Aggregation & The Three Mandatory Groups)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 16 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.14, into which three mandatory groups must an insurer divide each portfolio of insurance contracts?
options: 1. Life policies; 2. Non-life policies; 3. Health policies.
1. Male policyholders; 2. Female policyholders; 3. Minor policyholders.
1. Contracts onerous at initial recognition; 2. Contracts with no significant possibility of becoming onerous; 3. Remaining contracts in the portfolio.
1. Direct sales; 2. Broker sales; 3. Bank branch sales.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 16 mandates dividing portfolios into at least three distinct profitability cohorts at initial recognition to prevent blending onerous contracts with highly profitable ones.
explanationIncorrect: Cohorts cannot include contracts issued more than one year apart (the annual cohort requirement under Para 22).

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.16 (Annual Cohort Requirement under Para 22)
question: What is the 'Annual Cohort' rule under Ind AS 117 Para 22 that the Auditing Actuary must verify?
options: The insurer must reissue all policy documents annually on 1st January.
All policyholders must attend an annual general meeting once every 365 days.
Premium rates must increase by a flat 10% every calendar year.
A group of insurance contracts shall not include contracts issued more than one year apart.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 22 explicitly prohibits grouping contracts issued more than one year apart, ensuring that CSM release reflects the specific vintage and profitability of each annual cohort.
explanationIncorrect: Blending multiple years into an open-ended multi-year cohort violates Ind AS 117 aggregation standards.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 4.18 (Reinsurance Contracts Held: Net Cost vs Net Gain)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Paras 60-70 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.18, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate the CSM of a Reinsurance Contract Held?
options: Reinsurance recoveries can be recognized as cash in bank before treaties are executed.

The CSM represents the net cost or net gain of purchasing reinsurance; a net cost is recognized over the reinsurance coverage period, and a loss-recovery component is recognized if underlying contracts are onerous.
Reinsurance held must always have a zero balance sheet value under Indian law.
Reinsurance liabilities are directly netted against gross claims without separate valuation.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117, reinsurance held is accounted for completely separately from gross underlying liabilities; the reinsurance CSM reflects the cost of cover, with loss-recovery tracking for onerous gross contracts.
explanationIncorrect: Netting reinsurance assets against gross liabilities without separate disclosure violates balance sheet presentation rules.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.1 (Bottom-Up vs Top-Down Discounting Approaches)
question: How does FT-IGN 31 Section 5.1 and Ind AS 117 Para B78 guide the Auditing Actuary in evaluating discount rate methodologies?
options: Discounting is prohibited under Ind AS 117; all liabilities must be reported undiscounted.
Bottom-Up: Start with liquid risk-free yield curve and add an illiquidity premium; Top-Down: Start with reference asset portfolio yield and eliminate credit risk and market risk premiums.
Bottom-Up: Use inflation rate; Top-Down: Use the statutory corporate income tax rate.
Bottom-Up: Use the rate paid on savings bank accounts; Top-Down: Use the maximum interest rate charged on credit cards.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para B78, both Bottom-Up (risk-free + illiquidity) and Top-Down (portfolio yield minus credit/market risk) approaches are permitted, provided they reflect current market conditions.
explanationIncorrect: Both approaches should theoretically converge to reflect the liquidity characteristics of the insurance liabilities.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.3 (CCIL Zero-Coupon Yield Curve Verification)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.3, what must the Auditing Actuary verify regarding the CCIL Zero-Coupon Yield Curve (ZCYC)?
options: Confirm that the yield curve matches the interest rates published by commercial car loan dealerships.
Ensure that the yield curve is kept constant at a flat 8.00% across all 100 years.
Verify that the yield curve was hand-drawn by the insurer's chief economist.
Verify that the yield curve was sourced from the Clearing Corporation of India Limited as of the exact balance sheet date, correctly interpolated across liability durations.
explanationCorrect: In India, IRDAI and IAI guidance prescribe the CCIL Sovereign ZCYC as the primary reference risk-free curve; the actuary must verify date alignment, extrapolation methods, and interpolation accuracy.
explanationIncorrect: Using outdated yield curves or arbitrary flat discount rates distorts fulfilment cash flows.

question: When an insurer adds an illiquidity premium to the risk-free curve under the Bottom-Up approach, what must the Auditing Actuary challenge under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.5?
options: Whether the illiquidity premium increases the bonus paid to the investment team.
Whether policyholders signed a certificate confirming they do not need liquid cash.
Whether the illiquidity premium is higher than the inflation rate in the United Kingdom.

Whether the liability cash flows are truly illiquid (e.g. policyholders cannot surrender without severe penalty) and whether the calibrated illiquidity premium is objectively supported by market spread data.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.5, illiquidity premiums can only be applied to the extent liabilities possess illiquidity characteristics (e.g. non-surrenderable annuities vs highly liquid demand-surrender contracts).
explanationIncorrect: Applying high illiquidity spreads to liquid surrenderable policies artificially depresses reserves and violates Ind AS 117.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.7 (Risk Adjustment Techniques: Confidence Level vs Cost of Capital)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.7 and Ind AS 117 Para B91, what techniques may an insurer use to determine the Risk Adjustment (RA) for non-financial risk?
options: Guessing an arbitrary round number between 1% and 5% without any statistical modeling.
Setting RA equal to the statutory corporate dividend rate.
Using the exact astrology birth chart of the company's founder.
Techniques such as Value at Risk / Confidence Level technique, Tail Value at Risk (TVaR), or Cost of Capital technique, provided the method reflects entity-specific risk aversion.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 does not prescribe a single method for RA; common methods include VaR/Confidence Level, CTE/TVaR, and Cost of Capital, reflecting the compensation required for uncertainty.
explanationIncorrect: Regardless of the technique chosen, Para 119 mandates disclosing the confidence level equivalent corresponding to the results.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.9 (Mandatory Disclosure of Equivalent Confidence Level)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 119 and FT-IGN 31 Section 5.9, what disclosure is mandatory if an insurer uses the Cost of Capital method to determine its Risk Adjustment?
options: The insurer must disclose the confidence level corresponding to the results of that technique (e.g. 'RA corresponds to an 85th percentile confidence level').
The insurer must publish its proprietary computer source code in the official government gazette.
The insurer must disclose the personal salary of every actuary in the reserving department.
No disclosure is required if the method is approved by the statutory auditor.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 119 explicitly requires disclosure of the confidence level corresponding to the results of whatever technique is used to determine the Risk Adjustment.
explanationIncorrect: Failing to disclose the equivalent percentile confidence level is a direct disclosure non-compliance under Ind AS 117.

question: How does FT-IGN 31 Section 5.11 evaluate diversification benefits recognized in the Risk Adjustment calculation?
options: Diversification can only be recognized if all policyholders live in the same apartment building.
Diversification benefits can be assumed to be 100%, reducing the Risk Adjustment to exactly zero.
Diversification benefits across portfolios can be recognized if consistent with the entity's risk management perspective, but the actuary must evaluate correlation assumptions and legal ring-fencing.
Diversification across different lines of business is strictly illegal under Indian accounting law.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.11, diversification reflects entity-level compensation for risk, but the actuary must scrutinize whether assumed correlations hold under stress and whether legal restrictions (e.g. participating funds) prevent fungibility.
explanationIncorrect: Overstating diversification benefits during stressed conditions leads to dangerously inadequate Risk Adjustments.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.13 (Auditing Ultimate Loss Ratios in General Insurance)
question: In auditing General Insurance claim liabilities under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.13, how does the Auditing Actuary evaluate Initial Expected Loss Ratios (IELR)?
options: Insist that loss ratios must always equal 100% across all lines of general insurance.
Challenge whether IELRs reflect contemporary pricing shifts, rate increases, claims inflation, and underwriting changes, rather than blindly relying on outdated historical loss ratios.
Assume that all future claims will be exactly 0% due to advancements in artificial intelligence.
Accept management's budget loss ratio without question because management knows best.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.13, the Auditing Actuary must independently benchmark IELRs against rate changes, claims inflation, and emerging experience, particularly in long-tail lines (Motor TP, Liability).
explanationIncorrect: Using optimistic pricing loss ratios without empirical support causes material under-reserving in Bornhuetter-Ferguson models.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.15 (Claims Development Triangles & Tail Factors)
question: What audit procedures must the Auditing Actuary execute on claims development triangles under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.15?
options: Replace all historical claims data with computer-generated random numbers.
Delete the most recent 3 accident years if claims experience was unprofitable.
Color the spreadsheet cells in alternating blue and yellow patterns.
Verify data completeness against accounting ledgers, test triangle reconciliation, evaluate stability of link ratios, and scrutinize extrapolated tail factors.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.15, standard actuarial audit procedures include reconciling triangles to general ledgers, testing for diagnostic shifts (speed of settlement, case reserve adequacy), and testing tail extrapolation sensitivity.
explanationIncorrect: Unjustified manipulation of tail factors or link ratios constitutes audit distortion.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.17 (Evaluating Claims Inflation in Long-Tail Liability Lines)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.17, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate assumptions regarding medical, judicial, and wage inflation in Motor Third Party liability claims?
options: Assume inflation is zero because the Reserve Bank of India has an inflation target of 4%.
Apply a negative inflation rate of -10% per annum to reduce reported liabilities.
Inflation in insurance claims is a legal fiction that actuaries are forbidden from considering.
Explicitly evaluate whether inflation assumptions account for rising tribunal awards, medical cost escalation, and legal cost trends, rather than relying solely on general Consumer Price Index (CPI).
explanationCorrect: Judicial awards in Motor Third Party claims historically escalate at rates significantly above headline CPI; FT-IGN 31 Section 5.17 mandates rigorous challenge of claims-specific inflation assumptions.
explanationIncorrect: Failing to account for super-imposed judicial inflation causes catastrophic reserving deficits in casualty lines.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 5.19 (Onerous Contract Grouping at Annual Cohort Level)
question: An insurer attempts to avoid recognizing an onerous contract loss by pooling a loss-making commercial liability product with a highly profitable personal motor portfolio. How does FT-IGN 31 Section 5.19 evaluate this?
options: It is fully compliant because all insurance policies are signed on paper in India.
It is acceptable provided the company's statutory auditor owns shares in both portfolios.
It is permissible if the insurer pays a special pooling fee to the IRDAI.
It is strictly non-compliant; contracts subject to different risks and managed separately cannot be grouped into the same portfolio under Ind AS 117 Para 14.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 14, a portfolio comprises contracts subject to similar risks and managed together. Blending dissimilar commercial and personal lines to mask onerous contracts violates fundamental aggregation rules.
explanationIncorrect: Inappropriate portfolio boundary definitions to disguise losses is an audit red flag.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.1 (Auditing Actuarial Data Pipelines & PAS Feeds)
question: What is the Auditing Actuary's duty regarding data flows from Policy Administration Systems (PAS) to valuation engines under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.1?
options: Rely entirely on an oral confirmation from the IT helpdesk coordinator.
Verify data integrity, reconciliation of policy counts and financial totals between PAS, accounting ledgers, and actuarial models, and test automated ETL controls.
Demand that the insurer re-enter all policy records manually into Microsoft Notepad.
Assume that all computer databases are 100% accurate without conducting any data verification.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.1 and ICAI SA 500, the expert must test the accuracy and completeness of source data used in actuarial valuations, reconciling PAS feeds to audited general ledgers.
explanationIncorrect: GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out) applies to actuarial models; unverified data pipelines undermine all liability outputs.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.3 (Audit Testing of Model Specifications & Code)
question: How does the Auditing Actuary audit complex actuarial modeling software under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.3?
options: Delete all complex formulas and replace them with flat linear interpolations.
Perform independent specification reviews, benchmark sample policy calculations against standalone spreadsheets, and test model logic under boundary conditions.
Require the insurer to rewrite all actuarial software in assembly language.
Trust the software vendor's marketing brochure and conduct zero independent code checks.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.3 and APS 34 Section 2.10, the auditor's expert must validate model logic by independently replicating sample policies and verifying formulaic alignment with product filings.
explanationIncorrect: Independent sample policy verification is a core audit procedure under SA 620.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.5 (Change Control Logs & Version Control in Audits)
question: What must the Auditing Actuary verify regarding actuarial model change control logs under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.5?
options: Verify that all model modifications during the financial year were formally documented, tested, authorized by senior actuarial leadership, and evaluated for quantitative balance sheet impact.
Verify that actuarial model code was updated daily without any management authorization.
Ensure that previous model versions were permanently deleted with zero backup copies.
Confirm that passwords to the actuarial valuation system are publicly posted on the office whiteboard.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.5 and APS 34 Section 2.10.5, robust change controls must prevent unauthorized changes, document impact, and maintain full version histories.
explanationIncorrect: Uncontrolled or unauthorized model updates introduce massive risks of financial misstatement.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.7, why do Post-Model Adjustments (PMAs) or manual management overlays require intensive audit challenge?
options: Because PMAs are automatically exempt from all auditing standards under ICAI guidelines.
Because PMAs are outside automated system controls, prone to management bias, and can be used to manipulate reported profits or conceal model defects.
Because PMAs represent charitable donations made by the insurer to local hospitals.
Because PMAs can only be calculated by government tax inspectors.
explanationCorrect: PMAs represent manual spreadsheet overlays applied after core model execution. FT-IGN 31 Section 6.7 flags PMAs as high-risk areas susceptible to subjective manipulation and earnings management.
explanationIncorrect: The actuary must verify the governance, empirical justification, reversal criteria, and materiality of every PMA.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.9 (Audit Scrutiny of Management Expense Allocations)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65 and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.9, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate expense cash flows included in fulfilment cash flows?
options: Verify that only directly attributable expenses (acquisition and fulfillment) are included in contract cash flows, while non-attributable overheads (general marketing, IT development) are expensed in P&L.
Assign all company expenses exclusively to the term insurance portfolio.
Exclude all expenses completely, assuming that insurance companies operate with zero cost.
Allow all corporate expenses, including executive private jet leases, to be capitalized into insurance liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para B65 strictly limits fulfilment cash flows to directly attributable expenses. General corporate overheads cannot be loaded into liabilities to artificially inflate future CSM releases.
explanationIncorrect: Auditing expense allocation methodology and time studies is critical to prevent misclassification of overheads.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.11 (Treatment of Future Discretionary Benefits in Participating Contracts)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65(k) and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.11, how are future discretionary bonuses to participating policyholders audited?
options: Assume that management will never pay any future bonuses to policyholders under any circumstances.
Exclude all bonuses because discretionary items can never be audited under Indian law.
Verify that cash flows include expected future discretionary bonus payments, reflecting management's past practice, economic conditions, and policyholder reasonable expectations (PRE).
Set future bonus rates equal to the interest rate on 30-year US Treasury bonds.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 and Indian actuarial practice, cash flows must reflect expected discretionary payments within the contract boundary, taking into account statutory sharing rules (e.g. 90:10 gate) and PRE.
explanationIncorrect: Arbitrarily zeroing future bonuses distorts participating liability valuation and violates policyholder expectations.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.13 (Auditing Reinsurance Credit Risk / Non-Performance Default)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 63 and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.13, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate the allowance for reinsurer non-performance risk?
options: Verify that estimates of future reinsurance cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for credit default / non-performance risk based on reinsurer financial strength ratings.
Deduct an arbitrary 50% penalty from all reinsurance recoveries regardless of reinsurer solvency.
Ignore reinsurer default risk unless the reinsurer has already filed for bankruptcy.
Assume that all reinsurers will always honor 100% of claims with zero risk of default or dispute.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 63 explicitly mandates that reinsurance assets reflect the effect of the risk of non-performance by the issuer of the reinsurance contract, including collateral and credit ratings.
explanationIncorrect: Omitting reinsurer credit risk overstates the carrying value of Reinsurance Contracts Held.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.15 (Auditing Transition Methods: FTM vs MTM vs FVM)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Appendix C and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.15, what is the default transition method on initial adoption of Ind AS 117, and when may alternatives be used?
options: Management can freely choose whichever transition method produces the highest opening equity.
Fair Value Approach is the mandatory default for all Indian insurers without exception.
The transition method is decided by a majority vote of policyholders.
Full Retrospective Approach (FRA) is the mandatory default; Modified Retrospective Approach (MRA) or Fair Value Approach (FVA) can only be used if FRA is impracticable.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Appendix C mandates Full Retrospective Approach unless impracticable. Only when historical data gaps make FRA objectively impossible may an entity elect MRA or Fair Value Approach.
explanationIncorrect: The Auditing Actuary must rigorously test management's claim of 'impracticability' before permitting Fair Value or Modified Retrospective approaches.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.17 (Evaluating Fair Value Approach at Transition)
question: When an insurer uses the Fair Value Approach under Ind AS 117 Para C20 at transition, how does the Auditing Actuary audit the opening CSM?
options: Ensure that opening CSM is approved in advance by the World Bank.
Verify that opening CSM is determined as the difference between the fair value of the group (under Ind AS 113) and the fulfilment cash flows measured at the transition date.
Verify that opening CSM is set to exactly zero for all historical contracts.
Confirm that opening CSM is equal to the company's total historical premium collections since inception.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para C20, under the Fair Value Approach, opening CSM (or loss component) is the difference between fair value (exit price under Ind AS 113) and fulfilment cash flows at transition.
explanationIncorrect: The Auditing Actuary must evaluate the Ind AS 113 valuation model, cost of capital margins, and market participant assumptions.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.21 (Auditing Reinsurance Impairment under Ind AS 117)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 63 and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.21, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate potential impairment or dispute risk in Reinsurance Contracts Held?
options: Record reinsurance impairment only when the reinsurer's CEO issues a public confession.
Deduct 100% of all reinsurance assets, treating all reinsurers as fraudulent.
Assume reinsurance recoveries are risk-free assets guaranteed by the Central Government.
Verify that probability-weighted estimates of credit default and dispute haircuts are systematically calibrated using credit ratings, historical recovery delays, and collateral held.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 6.21 and Ind AS 117 Para 63, reinsurance recoveries must reflect expected losses from credit default and disputes, calibrated objectively against credit spreads and historical recovery rates.
explanationIncorrect: Ignoring reinsurer dispute or credit risk results in material overstatement of net insurance assets.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.23 (Premium Experience Adjustments vs Future Service)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B96 and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.23, how does the Auditing Actuary audit differences between expected and actual premium receipts during the year?
options: Premium variations are returned to policyholders as lottery prizes.
Experience adjustments relating to current or past service flow immediately to P&L; experience adjustments relating to future service unlock and adjust the CSM.
All premium variations are credited directly to general reserve in equity.
All premium adjustments are ignored until the entire policy terminates.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para B96 distinguishes between premium experience adjustments for past/current service (recognized in insurance revenue in P&L) and those relating to future service (adjusting CSM).
explanationIncorrect: Misclassifying premium differences distorts both current insurance revenue and future margin emergence.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.25 (Contract Boundary: Renewal Options and Paid-up Conversions)
question: How does the Auditing Actuary audit contract boundaries for policies with guaranteed renewal or paid-up conversion options under Ind AS 117 Para 34?
options: Verify whether the insurer has the practical ability to reprice the entire risk at renewal; if renewal premiums are contractually guaranteed, cash flows beyond renewal lie within the contract boundary.
Exclude renewal cash flows because policyholder choices cannot be audited.
Treat all options as having an infinite boundary spanning multiple centuries.
Assume the contract boundary ends on the 31st of December of the first policy year in all cases.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 34, cash flows lie within the contract boundary if the insurer cannot fully reassess risk and reprice the contract. Contractually guaranteed renewal rates bind the insurer within the boundary.
explanationIncorrect: Truncating contract boundaries when guaranteed renewal options exist leads to severe under-reserving.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.27 (Discount Rate Extrapolation: CCIL Sovereign Yield Curve)
question: Where insurance liabilities extend beyond 30 years (e.g. lifetime pension annuities) beyond the observable liquid G-Sec market, how must discount rates be audited under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.4?
options: Assume interest rates escalate by 5% every year indefinitely into the future.
Extrapolate by drawing a random freehand curve on a whiteboard.
Evaluate whether extrapolation to the Ultimate Forward Rate (UFR) follows prescribed IRDAI methodology, smoothly transitioning from observable CCIL market yields to the long-term anchor rate.
Assume interest rates drop to exactly 0.00% immediately after year 30.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 5.4 and IRDAI guidelines, discount curves for deep durations must use a structured extrapolation technique (e.g. Smith-Wilson) converging to the prescribed Ultimate Forward Rate.
explanationIncorrect: Arbitrary yield extrapolation introduces massive volatility into long-duration annuity liabilities.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.29 (Direct Attribution Criteria for Insurance Acquisition Cash Flows - IACF)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65(e) and FT-IGN 31 Section 6.29, which acquisition costs may be included in the measurement of insurance contracts?
options: Only acquisition cash flows directly attributable to the portfolio of insurance contracts to which the group belongs (e.g. selling, underwriting, and medical exam costs directly tied to issued policies).
Annual bonuses paid to the insurer's corporate board of directors.
General corporate advertising billboards in cricket stadiums and television branding.
Political campaign donations made by the insurance group.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para B65(e) restricts acquisition cash flows to costs directly attributable to issuing the portfolio. General brand advertising and corporate overheads are non-attributable and must be expensed as incurred.
explanationIncorrect: Capitalizing non-attributable marketing expenses violates Ind AS 117 and distorts contract margins.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.31 (Amortization of Insurance Acquisition Cash Flows Asset)
question: When an insurer pays acquisition cash flows before a group of contracts is recognized, how must the resulting asset be audited under Ind AS 117 Para 28A-28F?
options: Surrender the asset to the policyholder's bank account.
Recognize the asset as permanent goodwill that is never amortized.
Verify that the asset is recognized, tested for recoverability against expected future cash flows, and allocated to groups of contracts systematically as they are recognized.
Offset the asset against corporate tax liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Paras 28A-28F require recognizing an asset for pre-recognition acquisition costs, subjecting it to periodic recoverability impairment testing, and derecognizing it when the contracts are recognized.
explanationIncorrect: Failing to conduct impairment tests on deferred acquisition assets leads to fictitious asset inflation.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.33 (Auditing Fair Value Approach at Transition: Cost of Capital Calibration)
question: When auditing the Fair Value Approach under Ind AS 117 Para C20, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate the Cost of Capital rate used to determine market participant margins?
options: Use the inflation rate in Switzerland.
Use the statutory rate of return paid on postal savings accounts.
Verify that the Cost of Capital rate and required capital bases are calibrated objectively using observable Indian insurance market return expectations and IRDAI solvency regulations.
Accept any rate management chooses between 0% and 100% without documentation.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 113 and Ind AS 117 Para C20, fair value reflects an exit price; the Cost of Capital margin must reflect compensation required by a market participant under prevailing economic conditions.
explanationIncorrect: Using an unsubstantiated, depressed cost of capital rate artificially inflates opening equity at transition.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.35 (Investment Contracts with Discretionary Participation Features - DPF)
question: How does FT-IGN 31 Section 4.5 govern the audit of Investment Contracts with Discretionary Participation Features (DPF) under Ind AS 117?
options: They are reclassified as bank demand deposits under the Banking Regulation Act.
They must be audited under US GAAP Rule 404 rather than Indian standards.
They are completely exempt from accounting standards and require zero disclosures.
They fall within the scope of Ind AS 117 if the entity also issues insurance contracts; audited similarly to insurance contracts with contract boundary modifications under Para 71.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 3(c) and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.5, investment contracts with DPF issued by an insurer fall within Ind AS 117, ensuring consistent valuation of participating funds.
explanationIncorrect: Excluding DPF contracts from Ind AS 117 valuation distorts life insurer participating fund accounts.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.37 (Reversal of Loss Component in Subsequent Measurement)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Paras 49-52 and FT-IGN 31 Section 4.13, how is a subsequent favorable experience shift or assumption change applied to an onerous group of contracts?
options: The favorable shift is credited to opening retained earnings of the prior decade.
The favorable shift is paid out immediately as an executive cash dividend.
The favorable shift is allocated first to systematically reverse the existing loss component in P&L; only after the loss component is fully depleted does the group reinstate a positive CSM.
CSM is created immediately while leaving the loss component active on the balance sheet.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Paras 49-52, subsequent decreases in fulfilment cash flows allocate to reduce the loss component until it reaches zero; only excess improvements rebuild the CSM.
explanationIncorrect: Rebuilding CSM before extinguishing the loss component creates double-counting of profits.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.39 (Reversal of Loss-Recovery Component on Reinsurance Held)
question: When underlying onerous gross insurance contracts reverse their loss component, how must the corresponding Loss-Recovery Component on Reinsurance Contracts Held be audited under Para 66B?
options: Transfer the reinsurance recovery to policyholder bank accounts directly.
Write off the reinsurance contract as an expired treaty.
Retain the reinsurance loss-recovery component permanently as an unearned bonus.
Systematically reverse the loss-recovery component in profit or loss in tandem with the gross loss component, ensuring symmetry between gross and reinsurance accounts.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 66B establishes strict symmetry: when gross onerous losses decrease, the associated reinsurance loss-recovery component must be adjusted downwards in P&L.
explanationIncorrect: Maintaining an unadjusted reinsurance recovery component when underlying gross losses have reversed distorts net earnings.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.41 (Presentation of Insurance Revenue: Exclusion of Investment Components)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 85 and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.2, what major item must be strictly excluded from Insurance Revenue in the statement of profit and loss?
options: Reinsurance brokerage commissions paid in foreign currency.
Investment components (amounts an insurance contract requires the entity to repay to a policyholder even if the insured event does not occur, such as pure savings/surrender deposits).
The salary of the company's internal actuarial trainees.
Statutory corporate tax provisions paid to the government.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 85 prohibits presenting investment components (non-risk deposit refunds) in insurance revenue, eliminating historical top-line 'premium volume' inflation.
explanationIncorrect: Including deposit and savings inflows in insurance revenue violates core presentation standards.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.43 (Unbundling: Separating Distinct Goods or Non-Insurance Services)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 12 and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.4, how must the Auditing Actuary evaluate distinct non-insurance services bundled within a policy (e.g. roadside assistance, health concierge)?
options: Verify whether the promise to provide the good or service is distinct from the insurance contract; if distinct, unbundle and account for it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Demand that policyholders pay a second premium to the local municipal corporation.
Ignore the service and account for everything as a life insurance policy.
Cancel the insurance policy and treat the contract solely as a catering agreement.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 12 requires unbundling distinct goods and services that are not integrated with the insurance risk, measuring them under Ind AS 115.
explanationIncorrect: Failing to unbundle distinct services distorts insurance contract revenue and liability balances.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.45 (Bifurcation of Embedded Derivatives under Ind AS 109)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para 11(a) and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.6, when must an embedded derivative in an insurance contract be separated and audited under Ind AS 109?
options: When the economic characteristics and risks of the embedded derivative are not closely related to the host insurance contract and a separate instrument with the same terms would meet the definition of a derivative.
Whenever the policyholder resides in a foreign country.
Embedded derivatives can never be separated under Indian accounting law.
Whenever the policy is printed on glossy laminated paper.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 11(a) applies Ind AS 109 to determine whether an embedded derivative must be bifurcated and measured at fair value through profit or loss.
explanationIncorrect: Concealing non-closely related investment derivatives inside insurance contracts avoids fair value discipline.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.47 (Audit of Mutual Entities & Discretionary Residual Balances)
question: How does FT-IGN 31 Section 7.8 guide the audit of mutual insurance entities where policyholders own 100% of residual surplus?
options: Reclassify the mutual entity as a private commercial joint-stock corporation.
Assume mutual insurers are exempt from Ind AS 117 and need not keep accounts.
Verify whether all residual net assets are classified as insurance liabilities or equity based on contractual terms and governing mutual bylaws.
Distribute all mutual assets to the statutory auditors as an annual gift.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 7.8 and Ind AS 117, mutual insurers must analyze whether policyholder ownership of residual surplus requires classifying unallocated surplus as a liability to policyholders.
explanationIncorrect: Misclassifying policyholder residual rights distorts mutual entity balance sheets.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.49 (Risk Adjustment Allocation to Groups within a Portfolio)
question: Where an entity calculates its Risk Adjustment at the portfolio level, how must the Auditing Actuary audit the allocation of RA to individual groups of contracts under Ind AS 117 Para B90?
options: Verify that RA is allocated to groups of contracts on a systematic, rational basis that reflects each group's relative contribution to non-financial risk.
Set RA to zero in all groups by assuming zero risk.
Distribute RA randomly based on the alphabet of policyholder surnames.
Allocate the entire portfolio RA to a single small group to make all other groups appear profitable.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para B90 permits portfolio-level estimation of RA provided it is allocated to groups of contracts on a systematic and rational basis reflecting risk contribution.
explanationIncorrect: Arbitrary or biased allocation of RA to manipulate group-level onerousness constitutes audit non-compliance.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.51 (Auditing Claims Handling Expenses in Liability for Incurred Claims - LIC)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 7.10, what must the Auditing Actuary verify regarding Claims Handling Expenses (CHE) within the Liability for Incurred Claims (LIC)?
options: Assume claims can be settled with zero internal administrative cost.

Verify that internal and external claims management expenses (investigation, legal defense, claims adjusters) are explicitly included in fulfillment cash flows for all incurred claims (both reported and IBNR).
Deduct CHE from policyholders' bank accounts as an unexpected settlement fee.
Include claims handling expenses only if claims occurred more than 10 years ago.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65(f) and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.10, LIC fulfillment cash flows must include all direct claims handling expenses expected to be incurred to settle both outstanding reported claims and IBNR.
explanationIncorrect: Omitting claims handling expenses materially understates the Liability for Incurred Claims.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.53 (Currency Translation & Foreign Exchange Impact on CSM)
question: Where an Indian insurer issues policies denominated in foreign currencies (e.g. GIFT City IFSC branch), how is foreign exchange audited under Ind AS 117 Para 30 and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.12?
options: Insurance contracts in foreign currencies are treated as monetary items; exchange differences on fulfillment cash flows and CSM are recognized in P&L under Ind AS 21.
Foreign exchange variations are ignored by assuming all global currencies equal the Indian Rupee.
Foreign currency contracts are strictly illegal and cannot be audited in India.
Exchange differences are paid to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 30 and Ind AS 21, insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary items; foreign exchange changes on cash flows and CSM are recognized in P&L.
explanationIncorrect: Misclassifying foreign currency exchange shifts as CSM unlocking distorts foreign exchange gains/losses.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.55 (Interim Financial Reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B137 and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.14, what is the accounting policy choice available to Indian insurers regarding treatment of previous interim accounting estimates?
options: Interim reports are strictly forbidden for insurance companies under Indian law.
An entity must recalculate all interim periods from scratch using hindsight.

An entity may elect an accounting policy choice not to change the treatment of accounting estimates made in previous interim periods when applying Ind AS 117 in subsequent interim periods or annual reports.
Interim reports must be signed exclusively by the Ministry of Finance.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para B137 provides an accounting policy choice regarding whether previous interim period estimates are reversed in subsequent periods; the Auditing Actuary must verify that this policy is applied consistently.
explanationIncorrect: Inconsistent application of interim accounting policy choices across quarters distorts annual comparisons.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.57 (Mandatory Reconciliation Disclosures under Para 100)
question: What critical reconciliation disclosures must the Auditing Actuary audit in the notes to the financial statements under Ind AS 117 Para 100?
options: A list of all policyholder email passwords.
A reconciliation of the number of chairs and desks in the actuary's office.
Reconciliation disclosures are optional suggestions that insurers may omit.

Detailed reconciliations from opening to closing balances for the Liability for Remaining Coverage (LRC), Liability for Incurred Claims (LIC), and Contractual Service Margin (CSM), showing key drivers of movement.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 100 mandates comprehensive roll-forward reconciliations showing how insurance liabilities and CSM moved from opening to closing balance, detailing cash flows, revenue, finance expense, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Incomplete or missing roll-forward reconciliations constitute material disclosure non-compliance.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.59 (Cold Review Findings: Root Cause Analysis & Remediation)
question: When internal cold quality reviews identify recurring deficiencies in an actuarial audit engagement under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.2, what must the firm do?
options: Destroy the cold review report and pretend no deficiencies were found.
Conduct a root cause analysis, implement remedial actions (enhanced training, updated audit programs, mandatory partner re-briefing), and monitor effectiveness in subsequent audit cycles.
Dismiss the cold reviewer from employment for being excessively critical.
Increase audit fees by 50% to penalize the client for the audit firm's defects.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.2 and ICAI SQC 1, systemic audit defects identified during cold quality reviews require formal root cause analysis, corrective action plans, and firm-wide remediation.
explanationIncorrect: Ignoring cold review findings undermines audit firm quality controls and exposes the firm to disciplinary action by the QRB.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 8.4 (Audit Re-Performance Testing & Tolerance Thresholds)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.4, what is the protocol when the Auditing Actuary conducts independent re-performance of liability calculations?
options: Require the insurer to match the auditor's numbers to the exact single rupee, permitting zero variance.
Conduct re-performance only if the insurer pays an additional bonus fee.
Re-perform calculations on independent calculation platforms, establish pre-defined acceptable variance thresholds (tolerances), and thoroughly investigate any variance exceeding the threshold.
Accept any difference up to 50% of the company's total assets without investigation.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.4 and SA 620, re-performance testing requires clear pre-established tolerance limits; variances exceeding tolerance must be reconciled to identify underlying model or parameter causes.
explanationIncorrect: Ignoring differences that exceed established audit tolerances compromises the reliability of audit evidence.
